Bielsko-Biała (Bielsko) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bielsko-Biała, Poland

Not demolished. Bielsko's Jewish community, permitted to settle by an 1627 imperial edict but subject to shifting restrictions through the 18th century (including Empress Maria Theresa's 1752 cap of 88 families), organized independently in 1864; population reached 12.7% (1,660) by 1880. Until this cemetery's mid-19th-century founding, Bielsko's Jews were buried in nearby Cieszyn. Established following an 1849 cholera epidemic and transport ban, with burials documented from July 31, 1849, the cemetery gained a distinctive 1885 neo-Romanesque-Moorish funeral house by architect Karol Korn, featuring unique ceiling polychromes. Notable burials include Michael Berkowitz, secretary to Theodor Herzl, plus a WWI section for Jewish soldiers (memorial erected 1929) and even four Muslim soldiers who died in the same conflict. A 1930s Orthodox section was added. Postwar restoration removed German-language inscriptions from tombstones under government order; the cemetery became state property in 1963, was declared a historic monument in 1983, and returned to Jewish community ownership in 1997. The western section absorbed relocated remains and tombstones from the liquidated Biała cemetery.
